To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
quark effects do not spoil the IR cancellations in the gluon OPE coefficients and the one-loop logarithms are the most important power corrections in the dimension-four gluonic term of the OPE.

the one-loop quark contributions do not alter the cancellation of IR singularities in the OPE coefficients of the scalar gluebound correlator and that, therefore, the gluonic condensates are not altered.

the quark contributions to dimension-four gluonic OPE coefficients of the scalar glue-ball correlator are finite in the chiral (nf → 0) limit and, in the chiral regime, they do not alter the cancellation of IR singularities in the OPE coefficients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quark effects in the leading condensate term of the OPE for the scalar glueball.
the quark effects in the leading power corrections of the scalar gluebag correlation function.
the one-loop corrections to the OPE of the scalar glueballs, which are important for the determination of their masses and widths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quark effects do not alter the leading power corrections of the scalar gluebound correlation function in the gluonic condensates and, in particular, the one-loop quark effects do contribute to the dimension-four term in the gluonic OPE.
the gluon condensation is the leading power correction in the OPE of the scalar gluebal correlator, and that it is a very good approximation to the QCD sum-rule analysis.
the one-loop quark contributions are not relevant in the gluon-condensate OPE term of the scalar glueballs, and the gluon-condesate OPE is the leading power correction in the scalar glueball OPE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the one-loop logarithmically enhanced quark contributions in the dimension-four gluonic OPE term do not affect the sum-rules independent low-energy theorem.

the gluon condensation in the scalar glueball OPE does not change the leading order behaviour of the OPE and the one-loop logarithm contributions to the gluon condense term are the dominant condensate corrections.
the quark effects do not alter the IR behaviour of the dimension-four gluonic OPE term and, therefore, the IR behaviour of all OPE terms in the scalar glueball sum-rules.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the one-loop logarithmically divergent quark contributions are the dominant power correction in the gluon OPE coefficient, which is the main ingredient in the sum-rules analysis of the scalar glueballs.
the one-loop quark contributions do not alter the IR behaviour of the gluon condensation OPE coefficients.
the quark effects in the dimension-four gluonic term do not alter the leading power behaviour of the OPE.
